title: Terraform module: opinionated observability stack for VPC private deployments with upgrade hooks and health checks
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module for Redwood Private VPC deployments that provisions an opinionated observability stack: Prometheus (operator/helm), Grafana (helm chart + provisioning), OpenTelemetry Collector (otlp receiver + exporters), and log-shipping to our centralized log sink. The module must support safe in-place upgrades, pre/post upgrade health checks, remote state compatibility, and an upgrade hook mechanism to run migration jobs (Helm hooks or K8s Jobs) when changing chart versions or CRD upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Module can be instantiated with minimal required inputs and deploys Prometheus, Grafana, and OTel Collector into a provided cluster namespace
Supports overlay variables for private deployment constraints: node selectors, tolerations, network policy toggles, and private registry credentials
Implements a plan-time validation step that fails a terraform apply when incompatible helm chart upgrades are detected
Includes a controlled upgrade path: dry-run (helm diff), pre-upgrade health check, canary rollout option for Prometheus/Grafana, and post-upgrade verification
Health checks exposed as Terraform outputs and as Kubernetes readiness probes; module emits a summary status resource label for downstream automation
Logs are forwarded to Redwood central log sink (S3+prefix or existing Elasticsearch/Grafana Loki endpoint) and validated by a smoke log event produced during the Helm release
Module supports KMS-encrypted secrets (via Terraform provider) and documents IAM roles required for execution
Automated integration test (CD) that runs the module against a disposable EKS cluster, performs an upgrade path, and asserts metrics + logs continuity
tasks: Draft module API: variables, outputs, and opinionated defaults
Implement Helm provider resources for Prometheus operator and Grafana provisioning
Add otel-collector helm chart with OTLP receiver and configurable exporters
Implement log shipping using Fluent Bit/Vector to configurable sink
Build upgrade hook framework: terraform null_resource + local-exec calling helm diff / kubectl jobs
Create plan-time validation using terraform provider hooks and custom script
Add smoke tests: metrics scrape, grafana dashboard provisioning, test log event
Write docs and runbook: upgrade checklist, rollback steps, required IAM policies
Wire module into CI to run e2e tests on merge
acceptance_tests: Provision module in ephemeral cluster and wait for all pods to be Ready within 10 minutes
Query Prometheus for a synthetic metric created by the smoke job and assert value > 0
Open Grafana provisioning endpoint and verify default dashboards exist via API
Trigger a chart version bump and run upgrade path; verify no alerting gaps and logs persisted to sink
Validate that plan-time checks prevent an upgrade when CRD incompatible change is detected
notes: Prefer using upstream kube-prometheus-stack with pinned chart revisions and values overlay
Avoid enabling Alertmanager external integrations by default — leave webhooks configurable
We should centralize dashboard JSON in a config repo and provision via grafana provisioning
Discussed approach with Priya Nair (Reliability) and Liam O'Connor (Platform) — both prefer explicit upgrade windows and manual approval for major chart jumps
Consider adding a lightweight 'status' Helm chart that exports a single Kubernetes CR with overall stack health to be consumed by the Private control plane
